#   profile : profile name (fileserver, webapp, email, monitoring, devops, database,
#             office-worker, sales, developer, executive) -- or, for ai_guard_prompt
#             rows only, an AI Guard detector category (see below)
#   value   : URL (without https://), provider name, prompt text, or test name
#   enabled : yes | no  (optional — defaults to yes if column is absent)
# URL values: store without https:// prefix. The generator prepends https:// at
# script-build time. If you include https:// or http:// it will be stripped first.
# security_test rows: all applicable tests for each profile are listed explicitly,
# including disabled ones, so the full picture is visible before deployment.
# Enable or disable tests here, or toggle them via the in-script profile viewer.
# genai_provider / genai_prompt rows only appear for profiles that generate GenAI
# ai_guard_prompt rows: profile holds the AI Guard detector category being
# legal-advice, pii, prompt-injection, secrets, toxicity). A separate
# genai_provider block for the synthetic profile "ai-guard" lists which
# providers these prompts are sent to. These rows are prompts only -- no URLs,
# no file/image uploads -- and are consumed exclusively by the standalone,
# on-demand ai-guard-test.ps1 (generated via Windows Tools -> "Run AI Guard
# Prompt Tests"). They are never part of win-traffic.ps1 or the scheduled
# traffic-gen rotation, because AI Guard's per-category detection requires the
# authenticated user context that only a Zscaler Client Connector
# Blank lines and lines starting with # are ignored by the parser.
